root_cause.text: During NVMe controller reset, `nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set()` reallocates `ctrl->admin_q` without first releasing an existing admin `request_queue`, causing the previous queue object to be orphaned and leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ctrl->admin_q) blk_put_queue(ctrl->admin_q);` immediately before `ctrl->admin_q = blk_mq_alloc_queue(...)`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that on reset “a previous admin queue may still exist” and must be released to avoid orphaning it, noting this was a regression from commit `03b3bcd319b3` (“nvme: fix admin request_queue lifetime”).

intent_record.intent_summary: Release any existing NVMe admin queue before allocating a new one so resets or reinitialization do not orphan the old queue.
intent_record.what: A conditional check was added before allocating a new admin queue: if `ctrl->admin_q` is already set, the code now calls `blk_put_queue(ctrl->admin_q)` to release the existing queue, along with a comment explaining this is for the case where a previous admin queue remains from before a reset.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents an existing admin queue from being left orphaned when `nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set()` allocates a replacement queue. If the controller already has an admin queue, its reference is dropped before assigning a newly allocated one, avoiding a leaked or stale queue object during reset or reinitialization paths.

candidates.rationale: This allocates and assigns a new admin request_queue during reset/reinitialization without first releasing any existing ctrl->admin_q, directly causing the old queue object to be orphaned and leaked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement allocates a new admin request_queue and overwrites ctrl->admin_q during reset/reinitialization without first freeing any existing admin queue, which orphans the previous queue object and causes the leak described in the root cause.

The vulnerable construct is present in `nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set()`: it unconditionally allocates a new tag set and then assigns a new queue with `ctrl->admin_q = blk_mq_init_queue(set);` without first releasing any pre-existing `ctrl->admin_q`.
